rawItems.title: Cambs fraudster stole £40,000 from employer and spent it on skiing holiday
rawItems.content: A second-time fraudster has been jailed for stealing more than £40,000 from her employer and spending it on a skiing holiday. Kirsty Payne, 44, of Taverners Drive, Ramsey, admitted defrauding her Cambridge-based employer, Marshall Thermo King, which trades as Marshall Fleet Solutions. In February 2025, she processed a £400,410 payment through the company system—£40,383 more than the legitimate amount. The extra funds were traced to an account belonging to one of Payne’s family members. The discrepancy went unnoticed until April, when Payne was signed off work because of her deteriorating mental health. During a wellbeing check with the company’s head of HR, she suddenly confessed to the fraud and resigned. She first claimed the money paid for a relative’s medical treatment, but later told police it funded a skiing holiday in the French Alps. Payne said the theft was a "spur of the moment" decision. However, she had a previous conviction for fraud by false representation and said she was experiencing financial difficulties despite earning around £80,000 a year. Payne told officers she had been struggling mentally, especially due to a family member’s terminal illness. But she could not explain why she took the money. Detective Constable Valentin Radulescu, who investigated the case, said: "Payne gave little thought to the impact of defrauding her employer out of tens of thousands of pounds. rawItems.title: New 20-year Hunts parking plan set for debate as demand set to rise
rawItems.content: Huntingdonshire District Council's cabinet is set to discuss a new 20-year parking strategy aimed at supporting town centres, improving customer experience and planning for future growth. Huntingdonshire District Council’s cabinet will consider the proposed plan when it meets today (Tuesday September 15). Work on the new parking strategy began in early October 2025 after a procurement exercise. The strategy will run from 2026 to 2046 and focus on economic growth, customer service and future demand. It outlines a vision for a "well-managed, balanced and future-focused parking service" that supports economic growth while promoting integration with public transport, walking, cycling, and electric vehicle infrastructure. The strategy has four aims: supporting thriving town centres, delivering a modern service, linking parking to sustainable transport and managing its assets responsibly.
